about: Helen Keplinger is one of California’s most celebrated winemakers. A Smith College science graduate who chose UC Davis over medical school, she has made wine for Bryant, Grace Family Vineyards and Carte Blanche. Food & Wine named her winemaker of the year in 2012 and Vinous gave her the same title in 2023. She and her husband, DJ Warner, started Keplinger Wines in 2006 with a few hundred cases of Grenache and Syrah. Vermillion is their more accessible label: one Rhône-inspired red each year.

Vermillion is a blend of sites as much as grapes. It draws on small vineyards from Sonoma County to the Sierra Foothills, and the mix of varieties and sources changes with each vintage. The 2022 is 42% Grenache, 40% Syrah, 9% Petite Sirah, 4% Mourvèdre, 4% Graciano and 1% Cabernet Sauvignon, from a warm, dry year in Northern California that gave small, concentrated grapes. The previous vintage spent 16 months in French oak.

Expect blackberry, spiced plum and dark cherry with star anise, cocoa and a touch of lavender, rich but balanced. They suggest drinking it now through about 2032, served slightly below room temperature. Grenache brings the red fruit and warmth, Syrah the dark fruit and pepper, and the small share of Petite Sirah and Graciano adds colour and grip. It is a direct line to the style that made Keplinger’s single-vineyard Grenache and Syrah famous, at an everyday price.
